svg.title: FINN: public filings read once for everyone; your data below a line, seen by code only; your phone outside both, getting public facts and your own rows only
svg.desc: Solid parts run in this repo today; dashed parts are designed, not built. Above the line, every NSE filing and daily price, fetched by hand today, with a full year kept, flows into events (each filing stored once, a new revision only when a key detail changes), then is read and checked (rules settle most filings; a model reads the rest only once an API key is set, and code checks every reading), then into facts. A price-reaction study checks whether the filings FINN interrupts you for moved the stock; it audits the rules and never changes what the app shows you. Answering takes your question, on no-training terms, without your name or holdings, never kept, and finds quotes on a company's own earnings-call pages; no screen shows its answers yet. The app's snapshot, built by hand on 28 Oct from NSE and screener.in, is what the app serves; the app reading the ledger's facts instead is designed. Below a line, your side, code only: your book and the people you know, invented for the demo, matched to public facts by code with no model, inside a private project that is designed; the one read-only export of public facts into it is designed. Your phone sits outside both: public facts from the snapshot and, as designed, only what's yours. Planned for production, not deployed: events and facts in Cloud SQL, reading and answering on Cloud Run with Vertex AI, and the private side a locked project that can't call out, read only by your signed-in phone.

Public: what companies file, read once and shared by everyone

g.text: Filings and share prices
Everything companies file with the stock
exchange (NSE), plus each day's prices.
Fetched by hand for now. A year is kept.
pipeline/archive.py, pipeline/ingest.py
The price study
Looks back over a year: after a filing
FINN would alert you to, did the stock
move? It tests the rules. It never
changes what the app shows you.
evals/run_reaction.py
Events
Each filing is saved once. A new version
is added only if a key detail changes.
pipeline/ingest.py · SQLite
Read and checked
Rules sort most filings on their own. The
rest wait for a model, which needs an API
key. Code then checks the model's reading.
finn/ingest/steps.py
Facts
What FINN keeps from each filing: how
urgent it is, how big it is next to the
company's revenue, what results it
reports, and who it names.
finn/ingest/store.py

svg.text: your question

g.text: Answering a question
Looks for the answer in a company's
own earnings calls and quotes it. Your
question reaches a model without
your name or holdings, on terms that
forbid training on it, and it isn't kept.
The app has no screen for this yet.
finn/answer
The app's snapshot, 28 Oct
A copy of prices and filings I built by
hand from NSE and screener.in. The
app shows it, and can fetch one
company live when you ask. The plan
is to build it from the Facts instead.

g.text: What you hold and who you know
Code matches your shares and contacts to the public
facts, with no model. In this demo, all of it is invented.
finn/network
Your phone
Shows what changed in what you hold, and any company's page. You get the
public facts everyone gets, plus your own data, never anyone else's.
web/ on Vercel

svg.text: only what's yours
Outside both
public facts
For production I'd use Google Cloud (ADR 5, not deployed). Events and facts go in
Cloud SQL. Reading and answering run on Cloud Run with Vertex AI. Your private side
is a locked project that can't call out. Only your signed-in phone reads your data.
